title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: W is a basic localizer (localisateur fondamental) in (Cat), Hot(W) = W^{-1}(Cat), and A is a small category with its presheaf category A^ and the induced class W_A of weak equivalences in A^ (maps whose images under i_A : A^ -> Cat lie in W).

Corollaire 2. Finite products exist in Hot(W). Both canonical functors (Cat) -> Hot(W) and A^ -> Hot(W) commute with them, for A a strict test category. A marginal insertion sharpens the hypothesis: it suffices that A be totally W-aspherical. Since a W-test category gives Hot(W) ≃ W_A^{-1}A^, the corollary reduces to one claim. The localization functor A^ -> W_A^{-1}A^ commutes with finite products, i.e. the map Hom_{W_A^{-1}A^}(X, ∏Y_j) -> ∏ Hom_{W_A^{-1}A^}(X, Y_j) is bijective for every finite family (Y_j) and every X in A^.

Surjectivity, sketched. Represent each component as a 'roof' X -f_j-> Y'_j <-~- Y_j with Y_j -> Y'_j in W_A. Take f = (f_j) : X -> ∏Y'_j = Y'. This gives a map X -> ∏Y_j in the localization, provided ∏Y_j -> ∏Y'_j is in W_A. Stability of W_A under finite products is exactly what total W-asphericity (or strict test) provides; the next page states this.

The next page then formulates the characterization lemma, with these equivalent conditions:
(i) A is totally W-aspherical;
(ii) W_A is stable under finite products, or (ii bis) under -×Z;
(iii)/(iv) the localization functor commutes with finite products.
The surrounding pages treat injectivity. That needs a lemma amalgamating a finite family of weak equivalences out of Y. They also warn that componentwise homotopy f_j ~ g_j does not imply f ~ g without Kan-type hypotheses.

Purpose: show that the homotopy category of a strict test category is cartesian-compatible with Hot. This is the theory of strict test categories in the setting of an arbitrary basic localizer W.
errors: The surjectivity argument assumes every morphism X -> Y_j in W_A^{-1}A^ is a single roof X -> Y'_j <- Y_j with the weak equivalence pointing into the target. Without a calculus of fractions or a fibrant replacement (e.g. Cisinski's later model structure on A^), general morphisms are zigzags. This is a gap at this stage; it is partly addressed by the lemmas on the adjacent pages.

A minor point, implicit rather than wrong: ∏Y_j -> ∏Y'_j in W_A requires stability of W_A under products with an arbitrary Z (applied factor by factor), not merely asphericity of A. The note correctly identifies total W-asphericity as the needed hypothesis.

ideas.what: Hot(W) has finite products, and the functors Cat -> Hot(W) and A^ -> Hot(W) preserve them, for A a strict test (totally W-aspherical) category
ideas.modern_name: strict (W-)test categories; compatibility of localization with finite products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); systematized by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (sections on strict test categories / total asphericity), as circulated

ideas.what: Equivalence: totally W-aspherical <=> W_A stable under products (×Z) <=> localization functor commutes with finite products
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (strict test categories); Maltsiniotis 2005; Cisinski 2006

ideas.what: Surjectivity of Hom(X,∏Y_j) -> ∏Hom(X,Y_j) via roofs and product of weak equivalences
ideas.modern_name: products of weak equivalences / fibrant-replacement argument

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of known material: strict test categories and the preservation of finite products by the localization, for a general basic localizer. It was published and developed in Pursuing Stacks and in Maltsiniotis' and Cisinski's work. Nothing appears new.
transcription_corrections: Marginal insertion likely reads 'il suffit que A soit tot. W-asph.' (it suffices that A be totally W-aspherical), not 'il suffit de prouver que A est test.'
Left margin likely reads 'Mais on peut sans doute se passer de (Cat), et raisonner directement [dans A^]' rather than ending with 'directement A'.
'(A catégorie [-test-] stricte)' is correct: 'test' is struck through and then 'stricte' written.
